Open weights model tops coding benchmark

A research lab released an open weights language model on Tuesday that scored higher than several proprietary systems on a widely used programming benchmark, according to results published alongside the model card and reproduced by two independent groups.

The model was trained on a mix of licensed code, permissively licensed repositories and synthetic exercises. Its authors say the biggest gains came from a curriculum that gradually increased problem difficulty and from filtering out near-duplicate training files that inflated earlier scores.

Independent researchers cautioned that benchmark results can overstate real-world usefulness, because many test problems resemble code that appears online. They plan to evaluate the model on private, recently written tasks over the coming weeks before drawing firm conclusions.

The release includes inference code that runs on a single consumer graphics card with quantized weights, which several developers said would make the model practical for local coding assistants and offline use in regulated industries.
